title: Use Drupal database placeholders instead of concatenating SQL
summary: Drupal secure-code documentation says data must never be concatenated directly into SQL queries and directs developers to use proper argument substitution, select queries, escapeLike() for LIKE values, and fixed operator choices.

sources.locator: Use the database abstraction layer to avoid SQL injection attacks
sources.title: Writing secure code for Drupal

drupal_core.notes: This record reflects current Drupal secure-code guidance for database query construction.

actions: Use Drupal database placeholders or select() conditions for variable query values.
Escape LIKE wildcard input with the database connection escapeLike() helper.
Do not pass user input as a query condition operator.
checks: Review custom database queries for string concatenation of variable data.
Review LIKE conditions for escaped wildcard input.
Review dynamic query operators to confirm they come from fixed allowed choices.
evidence_requirements: Origin and trust level of query values and operators
automation_hints: Future static analysis can flag query() calls built from concatenated variables and condition operators derived from request input.

enforcement.rationale: The general rule is reviewed, but findings require project code evidence and data-flow context before enforcement.
